title: Tenant route journey wide-table and compact storage strategy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build a canonical, query-friendly tenant->route->journey wide table (invocation-level + compact session fingerprint) optimized for console analytics use cases (SLO and cost attribution, funneling, adoption signals) while minimizing storage and scan costs. We will replace existing scattered denormalized slices with a single compact wide-table plus a small set of targeted materialized views for heavy-peek queries. Goals: reduce end-user query latency for top Console dashboards, cut storage/scan costs by ~30% for monthly datasets, and provide clear lineage and incremental ingestion semantics.

Background: Current console telemetry is split across several event tables and nearline slices which cause expensive joins in dashboards and ad-hoc analysis. Existing materialized aggregates don't support multi-dimensional slicing (tenant, route, model variant, shard). This ticket designs the wide-table schema, ingestion pattern, compaction policy, and migration plan.

Proposed schema and storage decisions (high-level):
- Table name: console_analytics.tenant_route_journey_wide_v1 (logical).
- Partitioning: ingestion_date (DAY). Clustering: tenant_id, route_hash, invocation_hour. Sort key recommendation: (tenant_id, ingestion_date, route_hash, invocation_ts) for storage systems that support sort.
- Column selection: tenant_id, workspace_id, route_id, route_hash (64-bit), model_variant, invocation_id, invocation_ts, session_fingerprint (32-bit), action_sequence (compact varbyte encoding), tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, outcome_label, error_code, host_region, cost_estimate_usd, sdk_language, user_agent_family, exposure_flags. Keep high-cardinality telemetry as compact encodings (hashes, enums).
- Storage format: Parquet v2 with ZSTD level 5, and optional ORC for on-prem pipelines. Use bloom filters on route_hash and invocation_id where supported.
- Aggregation helpers: precompute HLL sketches for unique-invocations per tenant and tdigest for latency percentiles at daily granularity. Store sketches as binary blobs and expose SQL UDFs to merge/extract.
- Materialized views: three targeted MVs: tenant_daily_cost, route_latency_quantiles_by_variant, tenant_route_funnel_snapshots. Refresh window: incremental / streaming updates where possible; full rebuild weekly.

Ingestion and compaction plan: 
- Ingress: streaming collection into a raw event staging table with minimal transform.
- Transform: incremental MERGE job that upserts into tenant_route_journey_wide_v1 using dedup keys (invocation_id) and last-write-wins on invocation_ts. Use watermarking for late-arriving events (+72h).
- Compaction: weekly micro-compaction that collapses action_sequence arrays and removes tombstones. Implement a delta-merge pattern to avoid full rewrites.

Query patterns and optimization rationale:
- Frequent queries: per-tenant daily cost + top-10 routes by cost, per-route P95 latency by model variant, funnel step conversion rates. Cluster on tenant_id & route_hash to prune scans. Keep tokens and action_sequence compact to reduce row size.
- Trade-offs: storing sketches (HLL/tdigest) adds storage but reduces compute for approximate analytics. Using hashes for high-card columns removes cardinality but preserves groupability.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before merging):
- SQL-based sample dashboards (cost, latency, adoption) run under target latency targets (95th percentile < 3s for typical slices) against a month of synthetic data.
- Ingestion job successfully upserts streaming test events with deduplication and handles late events within 72h.
- Estimated monthly storage and query scan cost shows >=20% savings vs current baseline (benchmarks attached).
- Lineage documented in Confluence with mapping from old tables to new columns and a migration runbook.
- Rollout plan with toggle (console feature flag) to switch dashboards to new tables and back.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Lossy hashing could cause low-level attribution collisions for very high-card tenants. Mitigation: Provide optional un-hashed columns for customers flagged as high-sensitivity and fall back to exact keys for enterprise-tier tenants.
- Risk: Sketches add complexity to joins with other datasets. Mitigation: provide helper UDFs and pre-aggregated export for external use.

Open decisions (needs engineering/PM/ops sign-off):
- Final compression and bloom-filter config (Parquet ZSTD knobs) — list of recommended defaults provided in Confluence.
- Whether to use ORC for private on-prem pipelines only or as a general storage option.
- Exact retention and compaction cadence for the wide-table (30/90/365 days trade-offs).

Related documents and artifacts: see attachments.

Next steps: Prototype with 30 days of synthetic console events in dev BigQuery, run dashboard latency and cost comparisons, iterate on schema based on queries that perform worst. Migration window planning in coordination with Analytics and Console PMs.
